rituals.title: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
rituals.win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Repair”; release extra blame.
• Pulled back? Touch “Check The Whole”.
• “Find Your Slice” keeps blame in proportion.
• Compare “Imagine A Pie” with “Choose Repair”.
• I can use “Share The Slices” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
rituals.goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.
rituals.win: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Select Direction”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Name Likely”.
• “Name Likely” keeps meaning in motion.
• Compare “Picture” with “Select Direction”.
• I can use “Make Room” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture → Make Room → Name Likely → Select Direction
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose safety over values exercises during acute crisis or impairment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.steps:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
rituals.win: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Next”; release the score.
• Restart detected: “Reopen Choice”.
• “Reopen Choice” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Compare “Close Door” with “Choose Next”.
• I can use “Read Protest” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pretend closure for urgent, coercive, unsafe, or irreversible choices.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
rituals.goal: When the path is missing, choose the way of walking.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Quality — Ask: ‘What quality do I want this the action you can take now to carry?’ Pick one—honesty, courage, care, fairness, patience.
2. Look Single — Define how that quality would look in a single visible movement today.
3. Let Certainty — Let certainty remain absent while the compass gives direction.
rituals.win: ✓ Certainty stayed missing. Direction did not.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Certainty”; keep the compass.
• On return: “Look Single”.
• “Look Single” keeps meaning in motion.
• Compare “Ask Quality” with “Let Certainty”.
• I can use “Look Single” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Quality → Look Single → Let Certainty
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Recheck practical facts when uncertainty involves significant legal, financial, or health risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD
rituals.goal: Some solutions survive only because their costs stay hidden.
rituals.steps:
1. Use Control — Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, extra certainty, overworking.
2. Picture Short — Beside each, picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
3. Focus On Costs — Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
4. Choose Experiment — Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.
rituals.win: ✓ One hidden control-cost just lost today’s payment.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Experiment”; leave it unanswered.
• Shortcut: “Focus On Costs”, once.
• “Focus On Costs” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• At “Choose Experiment”, compare “Use Control”.
• I can use “Picture Short” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Use Control → Picture Short → Focus On Costs → Choose Experiment
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not remove prescribed treatment or essential safety behaviour without professional advice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MORE THAN THIS STATE
rituals.goal: A single moment cannot legally seize your whole identity.
rituals.steps:
1. Carry Qualities — Name three roles you carry, two qualities others have witnessed, and one state present today.
2. Imagine Large — Imagine a large Focus on around all six.
3. Place Painful — Place the current painful content inside, not across, the boundary.
4. Ask Part — Ask which part of the larger system should lead the one simple action.
rituals.win: ✓ This state stayed one part of me, not the whole system.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Part”; release extra load.
• Shortcut: “Place Painful”, once.
• “Place Painful” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• What changed: “Carry Qualities” → “Ask Part”?
• I can use “Imagine Large” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Carry Qualities → Imagine Large → Place Painful → Ask Part
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use simple grounding instead if expansion feels abstract or dissociative.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE THIRD VOICE
rituals.goal: Emotion and logic are witnesses; wisdom gives the final answer.
rituals.steps:
1. Open Voices — Complete three lines.
2. Name Feeling — FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. Name Facts — FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
4. Build Wisdom — WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Use Wisdom — Read only the third line before acting.
rituals.win: ✓ Emotion stayed real; the verdict became negotiable.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Use Wisdom”; let feeling settle.
• On return, repeat “Name Facts”.
• “Build Wisdom” separates feeling from fact.
• Compare “Open Voices” with “Use Wisdom”.
• I can use “Name Feeling” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Open Voices → Name Feeling → Name Facts → Build Wisdom → Use Wisdom
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Delay major action if either witness is too impaired to give usable information.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHAT JOB IS THIS FEELING DOING?
rituals.goal: An emotion is a messenger with several departments.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Separately — Ask three questions separately: What change is it signalling?
2. Prepare Action — What action is it preparing?
3. Communicating — What is it communicating to others?
4. Keep Concrete — Keep answers concrete.
5. Use the Message — Use the information. Keep the behaviour under your supervision.
rituals.win: ✓ The feeling delivered its message without taking over behaviour.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Use the Message”; let feeling settle.
• Pulled back? Touch “Communicating”.
• “Keep Concrete” separates feeling from fact.
• “Ask Separately” to “Use the Message”: what loosened?
• I can use “Prepare Action” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Separately → Prepare Action → Communicating → Keep Concrete → Use the Message
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not overanalyse when regulation or immediate safety comes first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CHECK THE BIOLOGICAL VOLUME KNOBS
rituals.goal: Sometimes the mind is loud because the body is missing basic care.
rituals.steps:
1. Review — Review five amplifiers: illness or pain; missed food or hydration; substances or withdrawal; sleep debt; movement deficit or excess.
2. Identify Strongest — Spot the strongest correctable factor.
3. Make Health — Make one health-supporting adjustment before treating the entire reaction as psychological truth.
rituals.win: ✓ The body got basic care before the mind got blamed.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Make Health”; no forcing.
• Re-entry move: “Identify Strongest”.
• “Identify Strongest” keeps sensation as data.
• Keep one lesson: “Review” → “Make Health”.
• I can use “Identify Strongest” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Review → Identify Strongest → Make Health
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, medication concerns, or dangerous withdrawal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PRELIVE THE HARD MOMENT
rituals.goal: Rehearsal can give the future a familiar exit.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture — Picture the trigger beginning.
2. Use Obstacle — Insert the exact skill you will use, the obstacle most likely to interrupt it, and your recovery if that obstacle wins once.
3. Continue Scene — Continue the scene through a realistic ending—not a perfect one.
4. Place Physical — Then place one physical reminder where the event starts.
rituals.win: ✓ The target became human-sized.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Place Physical”; release the score.
• Re-entry move: “Continue Scene”.
• “Continue Scene” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Picture” → “Place Physical”: what changed?
• I can use “Use Obstacle” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture → Use Obstacle → Continue Scene → Place Physical
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep imagery brief if anticipation escalates instead of preparing you.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FEELING OR FIXING?
rituals.goal: Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.
rituals.steps:
1. Drop Define — After body alarm drops, define the obstacle without emotional adjectives.
2. Ask Whether — Ask if one specific action could change it.
3. Choose Action — If yes, choose and schedule that action.
4. Return Acceptance — If no, return to acceptance or support.
5. Stop Soothing — Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key.
rituals.win: ✓ Soothing stopped where a real key was needed. The next move became practical.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Stop Soothing”; no breath-holding.
• Skip replay; use “Choose Action”.
• “Return Acceptance” — alarm isn’t command.
• What changed: “Drop Define” → “Stop Soothing”?
• I can use “Ask Whether” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Drop Define → Ask Whether → Choose Action → Return Acceptance → Stop Soothing
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid problem-solving while too activated to assess consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FINISH THE LOOK
rituals.goal: Defence narrows the world; orientation in the present reopens it.
rituals.steps:
1. Let Eyes — Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Scan Left — Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name Cues — Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow Neck — Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now.
rituals.win: ✓ Now is back in the foreground.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Place Attention”; no forcing.
• If it flares, choose “Name Cues”.
• “Allow Neck” keeps sensation as data.
• Before/after: “Let Eyes” → “Place Attention”.
• I can use “Scan Left” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Let Eyes → Scan Left → Name Cues → Allow Neck → Place Attention
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid head movement with injury, dizziness, or driving.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE DROP, NOT THE OCEAN
rituals.goal: One drop can teach what the ocean would drown.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Tiniest — Choose the tiniest fragment of the difficult material: one edge, colour, word, or body sensation.
2. Return Fully — Contact it briefly, then return fully to a stabilising cue.
3. Find Dose — Hold the dose that allowed recovery.
4. Use Less — Next practice uses the same or less—not an ambitious leap.
rituals.win: ✓ I touched one drop of the feeling without turning it into the ocean.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Use Less”; no forcing.
• Pulled back? Touch “Find Dose”.
• “Find Dose” keeps sensation as data.
• What lost power: “Choose Tiniest” → “Use Less”?
• I can use “Return Fully” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Tiniest → Return Fully → Find Dose → Use Less
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek trained support when even minimal contact overwhelms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
rituals.goal: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.
rituals.steps:
1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient.
rituals.win: ✓ One useful ingredient found; the rest can stay off the recipe.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Add Ingredient”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Ask Memory”.
• “Ask Memory” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Locate Bodily” to “Add Ingredient”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Boundaries” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Locate Bodily → Describe Boundaries → Ask Memory → Add Ingredient
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose an external anchor if internal tracking feels inaccessible or unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MAP YOUR OPERATING WINDOW
rituals.goal: Know the edges before you cross them.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Zones — Picture three operating zones: TOO HIGH, WORKABLE, TOO LOW.
2. Add Earliest — Add your earliest personal signs in body, speech, attention, and behaviour.
3. Picture Fastest — Beside each outer zone, picture the fastest safe route toward the middle.
4. Place Others — Place the imagined path where others can help recognise it.
rituals.win: ✓ Past and present are separate rooms again.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Place Others”; orient to now.
• Pulled back? Touch “Picture Fastest”.
• “Picture Fastest” moves memory toward then.
• What changed: “Imagine Zones” → “Place Others”?
• I can use “Add Earliest” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Zones → Add Earliest → Picture Fastest → Place Others
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use professional guidance when shutdown, mania, trauma, or severe loss of steadiness is involved.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
rituals.goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
rituals.steps:
1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.
rituals.win: ✓ The thought moved from identity to object.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Witness Motion”; watch the thought.
• Pulled back? Touch “Start”.
• “Let Body” proves thought is observable.
• Before/after: “Follow Breaths” → “Witness Motion”.
• I can use “Leave Breath Alone” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use outward sensory contact if breath attention increases panic or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RHYTHM BEFORE DEPTH
rituals.goal: Rhythm first. Depth can follow.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Slow — Choose a slow, comfortable pace in which inhale and exhale feel smooth.
2. Use Quiet — Use a quiet timer or gentle movement as metronome, never forcing lung volume.
3. Continue Long — Continue long enough to find a repeatable rhythm, then remove the metronome and keep one easy cycle.
rituals.win: ✓ Motion replaced the waiting game.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Long”; then keep moving.
• On return, repeat “Use Quiet”.
• “Use Quiet” proves motion is available.
• What lost power: “Choose Slow” → “Continue Long”?
• I can use “Use Quiet” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Slow → Use Quiet → Continue Long
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Abandon pacing if it feels restrictive or medically unsuitable.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE EVEN BRIDGE
rituals.goal: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.
rituals.win: ✓ Noise separated into something the mind can hold.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Complete Few”; then keep moving.
• Skip replay; use “Imagine Pair”.
• “Imagine Pair” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Pick Requires” → “Complete Few”.
• I can use “Count Exhale” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Pick Requires → Count Exhale → Imagine Pair → Complete Few
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Return to spontaneous breathing if equality creates pressure.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BREATHE THE GESTURE
rituals.goal: Give respiration a visible partner.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Slow — Take one slow movement with two directions—arms open and close, rise and lower, reach and return.
2. Return Direction — Pair the expansive direction with inhale and the returning direction with exhale.
3. Let Movement — Let movement size follow comfort, then complete one cycle without conscious pairing.
rituals.win: ✓ The task lost enough weight to begin.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Movement”; then keep moving.
• Skip replay; use “Return Direction”.
• “Return Direction” proves motion is available.
• Look back: “Choose Slow” → “Let Movement”.
• I can use “Return Direction” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Slow → Return Direction → Let Movement
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Modify for pain, balance issues, fatigue, or mobility limits.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
rituals.goal: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.
rituals.win: ✓ The social scoreboard stopped being the whole room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Hold Conclusions”; drop the scoreboard.
• Skip replay; use “Ask Claims”.
• “Ask Claims” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Difference check: “Picture Appears” → “Hold Conclusions”.
• I can use “Ask Claims” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Appears → Ask Claims → Hold Conclusions
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Discontinue if sleep-related inquiry worsens insomnia or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES
rituals.goal: Stability is trained before the verdict arrives.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Action — Imagine the action succeeding.
2. State Governing — State what that value asks of you next.
3. Imagine Failing — Imagine it failing.
4. State Value — State how the same value responds there.
5. Let Outcome — Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.
rituals.win: ✓ Meaning found a next move without denying the pain.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Outcome”; keep both sides.
• Pulled back? Touch “Imagine Failing”.
• “State Value” widens the evidence field.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Action” → “Let Outcome”.
• I can use “State Governing” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Action → State Governing → Imagine Failing → State Value → Let Outcome
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use equanimity to ignore grief, accountability, or material consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE
rituals.goal: Extremes can impersonate discipline.
rituals.steps:
1. Rest Review — Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find Area — Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set Middle — Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Choose Smallest — Use the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.
rituals.win: ✓ The ignored side regained a vote.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Smallest”; keep both sides.
• Return once to “Set Middle”.
• “Set Middle” widens the evidence field.
• Look back: “Rest Review” → “Choose Smallest”.
• I can use “Find Area” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Rest Review → Find Area → Set Middle → Choose Smallest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Medical and nutritional needs should override generic moderation advice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
rituals.goal: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.
rituals.steps:
1. Question Promise — Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Empty First — Do not organise while emptying.
3. Sort Entries — When the mind offers silence, sort entries into do, schedule, delegate, reference, or delete.
4. Choose Physical — Choose only the first physical action.
rituals.win: ✓ Mental countertop cleared. One physical move remains.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Choose Physical”; redirect attention.
• On return: “Sort Entries”.
• “Sort Entries” proves one signal leads.
• “Choose Physical”: what changed from “Question Promise”?
• I can use “Empty First” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Question Promise → Empty First → Sort Entries → Choose Physical
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Protect confidential material and avoid endless Name refinement.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE REQUEST SPINE
rituals.goal: Clear and firmness needs structure when emotion bends the message.
rituals.steps:
1. Describe Situation — Say the visible situation.
2. Express Impact — Express its impact.
3. Assert Request — Assert the exact request or no.
4. Reinforce Cooperation — Reinforce why cooperation helps.
5. Picture Sentence — Picture one sentence for each part, then deliver the leanest version.
rituals.win: ✓ The request kept its backbone and lost the extra weight.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Picture Sentence”; release extra load.
• Return once to “Assert Request”.
• “Reinforce Cooperation” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Before/after: “Describe Situation” → “Picture Sentence”.
• I can use “Express Impact” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Describe Situation → Express Impact → Assert Request → Reinforce Cooperation → Picture Sentence
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use support or distance when direct assertion could provoke danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING
rituals.goal: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.
rituals.steps:
1. Separate Unknown — Picture three separate statements: their behaviour; what effect it had; what you do not know about intention.
2. Base — Base your next boundary on behaviour and impact.
3. Leave Motive — Leave motive open until reliable evidence or direct communication updates it.
rituals.win: ✓ The need to know shrank below the need to live the next minute.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Leave Motive”; leave it unanswered.
• Use “Base” on return.
• “Base” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Separate Unknown” versus “Leave Motive”: what eased?
• I can use “Base” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Separate Unknown → Base → Leave Motive
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use uncertainty about motive to postpone urgent protection.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED
rituals.goal: Other minds are opaque until they speak and behave.
rituals.steps:
1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.
2. Replace Possibilities — Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
3. Possibility — Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence.
4. Choose Behaviour — Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active.
rituals.win: ✓ Curiosity stayed open without pretending I could read another mind.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Behaviour”; soften the jaw.
• Catch restart with “Possibility”.
• “Possibility” keeps clarity above heat.
• What lost power: “Catch Sentence” → “Choose Behaviour”?
• I can use “Replace Possibilities” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Catch Sentence → Replace Possibilities → Possibility → Choose Behaviour
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Trust documented patterns when direct questioning is unsafe or repeatedly manipulated.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
rituals.goal: Two competing experiences can become one pattern.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Signals — Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
2. Alternate B — Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
3. Hold Time — Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
4. Decide After — Decide only after the braid is complete.
rituals.win: ✓ Two competing signals became one braid I could actually read.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Decide After”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Hold Time”.
• “Hold Time” proves one signal leads.
• Compare “Choose Signals” with “Decide After”.
• I can use “Alternate B” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Signals → Alternate B → Hold Time → Decide After
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not braid a safety alarm with pressure to ignore it.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
rituals.steps:
1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.
rituals.win: ✓ I matched the pressure, brought it back to zero, and checked what remained.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Reach Zero”; mark the pause.
• If it flares, choose “Step Down”.
• “Step Down” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What lost power: “Press Equal” → “Reach Zero”?

rituals.title: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
rituals.goal: Direct data can update the relationship model.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Assumption — Picture the assumption driving your reaction.
2. Question Whose — Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong.
3. Ask Suitable — Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model.

rituals.supports:

rituals.formula_flow: Picture Assumption → Question Whose → Ask Suitable
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TRANSLATE ACROSS SENSES
rituals.goal: A vague state can become workable in another medium.
rituals.steps:
1. Represent — Represent tension as a texture, a sound as a shape, or an emotion as colour and movement.
2. Make Translation — Make the translation concrete enough to Imagine or gesture.
3. Observe Whether — Alter one property in the new medium and observe if the first state changes.

rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COUNT EVERY OPEN LOOP
rituals.goal: Invisible commitments keep using memory until named.
rituals.steps:
1. Question Task — Name every unresolved promise, question, task, decision, and waiting item without solving any.
2. Use Line — Use one line each.
3. Imagine Boundary — When nothing else appears for thirty seconds, imagine a boundary around the inventory and choose a separate processing time.

rituals.safety:
PAUSE
End the capture if list-making increases overwhelm without containment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES
rituals.goal: Ideas, duties, fears, and memories should not share one queue.
rituals.steps:
1. Question Capture — Catch each mental item, then route it into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION.
2. Give Category — Give each category its own processing rule.
3. Don't Determine — Prioritise only after sorting, so emotional intensity does not determine inbox order.
rituals.win: ✓ The mind got separate queues instead of one emergency pile.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Don't Determine”; mark the pause.
• Shortcut: “Give Category”, once.
• “Give Category” proves choice interrupted habit.

rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WANT NOW / PROTECT LATER
rituals.goal: Desire and value need separate lanes.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Urge — Picture what the present urge wants, then what future life is worth protecting.
2. Name Cost — Name the cost each imposes on the other.
3. Choose Action — Choose one action that acknowledges desire while keeping the valued asset intact.
rituals.win: ✓ Desire stayed acknowledged while the future asset stayed protected.

rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PREVIEW THE AFTER
rituals.goal: Delayed reward is undercounted because the mind cannot feel it yet.
rituals.steps:
1. Protect Enjoyed — Picture a ten-second scene immediately after completion: what is lighter, available, learned, protected, or enjoyed?
2. Include Sensory — Include a sensory marker plus one practical consequence.
3. State Accessible — Begin the task while that specific after-state remains accessible.
rituals.win: ✓ Delay lost its claim on the next minute.

• One exhale after “State Accessible”; redirect attention.

• “Include Sensory” proves one signal leads.
• “State Accessible”: what changed from “Protect Enjoyed”?
• I can use “Include Sensory” amid noise.

rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not fabricate benefits that the action is unlikely to deliver.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE BORING DOSE
rituals.goal: Low stimulation can be trained in measured practice round.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Safe — Set up a boring task that is safe and preselect a short interval.
2. Remove Entertainment — Remove entertainment but keep necessary tools.
3. Stay Boredom — Stay with boredom’s body sensations until the timer ends, then stop even if you could continue.
4. Raise the Dose — Increase future doses slowly.
rituals.win: ✓ I took a measured dose of boring and proved I could stay.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Raise the Dose”; no breath-holding.
• Use “Stay Boredom” on return.

• Compare “Choose Safe” with “Raise the Dose”.
• I can use “Remove Entertainment” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Safe → Remove Entertainment → Stay Boredom → Raise the Dose
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Adapt for attention disorders and never use boredom as punishment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BUILD MEANING ON FIVE LEGS
rituals.goal: One collapsed source should not fell the whole table.
rituals.steps:
1. Rate Meaning — Rate meaning currently available through relationship, contribution, growth, experience, and transcendence.
2. Choose Weakest — Choose the weakest repairable leg and one small action that strengthens it.
3. Keep Strongest — Keep the strongest leg from carrying everything.
rituals.win: ✓ The present gained evidence the memory cannot overwrite.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Strongest”; orient to now.
• Skip replay; use “Choose Weakest”.
• “Choose Weakest” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Rate Meaning” → “Keep Strongest”?
• I can use “Choose Weakest” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Rate Meaning → Choose Weakest → Keep Strongest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pluralism to avoid repairing a central loss that needs care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHAT PREPARATION DID WORRY ACTUALLY PRODUCE?
rituals.goal: Imagined work should show a deliverable.
rituals.steps:
1. Create Worry — Name every concrete preparation created by the worry.
2. Separate Useful — Separate useful actions from repeated simulation.
3. Prepare Name — If the list contains a real gap, prepare once.
4. Remain Name — If no gap remains, label further worry UNPAID OVERTIME.
rituals.win: ✓ Worry produced no new deliverable. Overtime cancelled.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Remain Name”; orient to now.
• If it flares, choose “Prepare Name”.
• “Prepare Name” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Create Worry” → “Remain Name”?
• I can use “Separate Useful” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Create Worry → Separate Useful → Prepare Name → Remain Name
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss new information simply because worry has repeated.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MARK THE QUALITY DROP
rituals.goal: Analysis needs an exit before fatigue corrupts it.
rituals.steps:
1. Repeat No — Define your personal decline signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower comprehension, repeated searches, no new distinctions.
2. Stop Last — When two appear, stop and hold the last reliable conclusion.
3. Start Recovery — Recovery precedes any reopening.
rituals.win: ✓ I caught the moment thinking quality dropped and exited before fatigue took over.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Start Recovery”; keep both sides.
• On return: “Stop Last”.
• “Stop Last” widens the evidence field.
• “Start Recovery”: what changed from “Repeat No”?
• I can use “Stop Last” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Repeat No → Stop Last → Start Recovery
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Continue only when delay creates greater risk than reduced quality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
rituals.steps:
1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.
rituals.win: ✓ The worry cycle lost its automatic restart.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Fact”; orient to now.
• Use “Shift” on return.
• “Shift” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Recall Exchange” → “Keep Fact”?
• I can use “Halve Speed” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Recall Exchange → Halve Speed → Shift → Keep Fact
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if replay raises distress, becomes compulsive, or concerns abuse or danger that requires support and protection.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: GIVE THOUGHTS WEIGHTED VOTES
rituals.goal: Mental statements should not all receive one ballot.
rituals.steps:
1. Score Evidence — For each influential thought, score evidence, relevant expertise, recency, and decision relevance.
2. Multiply — Multiply nothing; simply rank.
3. Let Highest — Let the highest-quality thought advise the action while lower-ranked voices remain recorded but nonbinding.
rituals.win: ✓ The loudest thought lost the automatic deciding vote.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Highest”; orient to now.
• Use “Multiply” on return.
• “Multiply” moves memory toward then.
• Keep one lesson: “Score Evidence” → “Let Highest”.
• I can use “Multiply” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Score Evidence → Multiply → Let Highest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not confuse confidence, status, or repetition with expertise.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: AUCTION THE NEXT ATTENTION BLOCK
rituals.goal: Limited attention needs a clear way to choose.
rituals.steps:
1. Let Active — Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value.
2. Total — Total the four ratings.
3. Protect Block — Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires.
4. Update Evidence — Re-auction with updated evidence.
rituals.win: ✓ My next attention block went to the highest-value bidder.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Update Evidence”; slow the clock.
• Pulled back? Touch “Protect Block”.
• “Protect Block” puts facts above speed.
• Compare “Let Active” with “Update Evidence”.
• I can use “Total” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Let Active → Total → Protect Block → Update Evidence
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Emergency signals may override the auction immediately.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.goal: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
rituals.steps:
1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.
rituals.win: ✓ Five icons exposed the repeat—and one place to exit.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose An Exit”; end the lap.
• If it flares, choose “Spot The Return”.
• “Spot The Return” proves loops can stop.
• Look back: “No Sentences” → “Choose An Exit”.
• I can use “Imagine Five Signs” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: No Sentences → Imagine Five Signs → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
rituals.goal: Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.
rituals.steps:
1. Use Small — Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.
3. Move Object — Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration.
4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move.
rituals.win: ✓ The abstract problem moved on the table—and revealed a real-world move.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Name Real”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Move Object”.
• “Move Object” moves memory toward then.
• Look back: “Use Small” → “Name Real”.
• I can use “Feel Arrange” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Use Small → Feel Arrange → Move Object → Name Real
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not treat symbolic placement as factual evidence about other people.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
rituals.goal: The future gets easier when it already feels familiar.
rituals.steps:
1. Create Memory — Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include Time — Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look Backward — Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.
rituals.win: ✓ The future felt remembered enough for the first movement to become obvious.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Look Backward”; redirect attention.
• Catch restart with “Include Time”.
• “Include Time” proves one signal leads.
• At “Look Backward”, compare “Create Memory”.
• I can use “Include Time” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Create Memory → Include Time → Look Backward
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep future scenes realistic rather than using fantasy as avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
rituals.goal: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.
rituals.steps:
1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?
2. Ask Fear — What do you fear will happen?
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable?
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
rituals.win: ✓ Resistance revealed the need it was trying to protect.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Picture Negotiate”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Make Step”.
• “Make Step” moves memory toward then.
• “Give Obstacle” versus “Picture Negotiate”: what eased?
• I can use “Ask Fear” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Give Obstacle → Ask Fear → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not personify intrusive voices or experiences if that worsens symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
rituals.goal: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine The Parts — Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. See The Links — Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Find the Lever — Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Test It — Try that small change once.
rituals.win: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Test It”; mark the pause.
• Skip replay; use “Find the Lever”.
• “Find the Lever” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Imagine The Parts” versus “Test It”: what eased?
• I can use “See The Links” before autopilot.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine The Parts → See The Links → Find the Lever → Test It
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the mental picture simple. Stop if you begin analysing without taking action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR
rituals.goal: Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.
rituals.steps:
1. Create Figure — Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.
2. Give Posture — Give it posture, voice, and one signature behaviour.
3. Borrow One Move — Borrow only that behaviour for this situation. You do not need to become the character.
rituals.win: ✓ One useful move borrowed. The character can stay fictional.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Borrow One Move”; leave the forecast.
• Return once to “Give Posture”.
• “Give Posture” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Create Figure” → “Borrow One Move”: what changed?
• I can use “Give Posture” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Create Figure → Give Posture → Borrow One Move
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the avatar clearly imaginary and values-consistent.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BUILD THE MINIATURE FIRST
rituals.goal: A life change can be tested before full commitment.
rituals.steps:
1. Create Low — Create a low-risk scaled version: one-day routine, sample client, temporary location, trial budget, mock conversation.
2. State Prototype — State what the prototype must reveal and the maximum cost.
3. Test Miniature — Test Miniature it, collect feedback, and redesign before expansion.
rituals.win: ✓ I tested the miniature before asking the full-size life change to work.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Test Miniature”; watch the thought.
• If it flares, choose “State Prototype”.
• “State Prototype” proves thought is observable.
• What lost power: “Create Low” → “Test Miniature”?
• I can use “State Prototype” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Create Low → State Prototype → Test Miniature
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Check that the prototype is ethically and practically reversible.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT TIME ARROWS ON THE OPTIONS
rituals.goal: Choices change value while you wait.
rituals.steps:
1. Option — Notice every option as improving, stable, decaying, or expiring with delay.
2. Add Condition — Add the date or condition where its arrow changes.
3. Follow Time Arrows — Sequence decisions around genuine expiry rather than anxiety’s false deadlines.
rituals.win: ✓ I put time arrows on the options and found the real deadline.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Time Arrows”; watch the thought.
• On return: “Add Condition”.
• “Add Condition” proves thought is observable.

• I can use “Add Condition” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Option → Add Condition → Follow Time Arrows

PAUSE
Verify deadlines rather than assuming urgency.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
rituals.goal: Missing information must earn its collection cost.
rituals.steps:
1. Point Positive — For every desired data point, picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. Stop Collecting — If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Test Relevance — Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.
rituals.win: ✓ Asked what the missing fact could actually change before paying to collect it.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test Relevance”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Stop Collecting”.
• “Stop Collecting” moves memory toward then.
• Keep one lesson: “Point Positive” → “Test Relevance”.
• I can use “Stop Collecting” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Point Positive → Stop Collecting → Test Relevance
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep legally, clinically, or ethically required information even when choice impact seems small.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
rituals.goal: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.
rituals.steps:
1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.
rituals.win: ✓ I let two options enter each round until one earned the next move.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Crown Next”; release the score.
• On return, repeat “Play Pairs”.
• “Play Pairs” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Seed Options” → “Crown Next”?
• I can use “Pick Criterion” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
For high-stakes choices, use the winner only as the next research step and include qualified advice and all safety criteria.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
rituals.goal: Sunk cost is history, not future value.
rituals.steps:
1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Remove Sunk Vote — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.
rituals.win: ✓ The past investment stayed in history and lost its vote on the future.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Remove Sunk Vote”; slow the clock.
• On return: “Compare Options”.
• “Compare Options” puts facts above speed.
• At “Remove Sunk Vote”, compare “Hide Already”.
• I can use “Compare Options” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Hide Already → Compare Options → Remove Sunk Vote
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Account for contractual or reputational consequences that genuinely persist.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: IMAGINE THE FAILURE HEADLINE EARLY
rituals.goal: Imagine the plan failed so hidden pathways must speak.
rituals.steps:
1. Project — Project yourself after failure and name the three most plausible causes—not exotic disasters.
2. Add Prevention — For each, add one prevention, detection sign, or recovery step.
3. Update Commitment — Update the plan before commitment.
rituals.win: ✓ The bar came down to a level action can actually reach.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Update Commitment”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Add Prevention”.
• “Add Prevention” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What changed: “Project” → “Update Commitment”?
• I can use “Add Prevention” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Project → Add Prevention → Update Commitment
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not let pre-mortem become unlimited worst-case story generation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PROTECT THE VALID CHOICE
rituals.goal: Endless reopening can destroy good decisions after they are made.
rituals.steps:
1. Define — Establish the evidence threshold that would justify reconsideration.
2. Date Store — Store the rationale and first review date.
3. Name Post — When discomfort appears without qualifying evidence, name it post-decision noise and continue implementation.
rituals.win: ✓ Post-decision noise lost the power to reopen the choice.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Name Post”; release the score.
• On return: “Date Store”.
• “Date Store” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Define” → “Name Post”?
• I can use “Date Store” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Define → Date Store → Name Post
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reopen immediately for ethical, legal, health, or safety changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BREAK THE EXPECTED SEQUENCE
rituals.goal: Life scripts stay automatic until the next scene is questioned.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Culturally — Picture the culturally expected next step.
2. Name Benefits — Name who benefits, what value it serves, and what it costs you.
3. Generate — Generate one respectful alternative sequence.
4. Test Small — Test a small part without declaring war on the whole culture.
rituals.win: ✓ One alternate scene became possible without turning culture into the enemy.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Test Small”; keep both sides.
• Re-entry move: “Generate”.
• “Generate” widens the evidence field.
• Difference check: “Picture Culturally” → “Test Small”.
• I can use “Name Benefits” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Culturally → Name Benefits → Generate → Test Small
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Consider relationship and safety consequences, especially in restrictive environments.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: HIDE THE CROWD’S ANSWER
rituals.goal: Check fit before popularity enters the room.
rituals.steps:
1. Group Preference — Before seeing ratings, likes, rankings, or group preference, assess quality using your own criteria.
2. Hold Judgement — Hold the judgement and reasons.
3. View Crowd — Reveal social proof afterward and change your view only if the crowd supplies new evidence, not mere numbers.
rituals.win: ✓ Made the choice before the crowd’s answer entered the room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “View Crowd”; watch the thought.
• Return once to “Hold Judgement”.
• “Hold Judgement” proves thought is observable.
• Look back: “Group Preference” → “View Crowd”.
• I can use “Hold Judgement” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Group Preference → Hold Judgement → View Crowd
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use expert consensus appropriately where specialised knowledge matters.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
rituals.goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.
rituals.steps:
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.
